questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I picked my exchange destination based on my personal excitement about the Dutch culture, especially the lively Dutch way of life. The Dutch are known for their rich history and cool attitudes, while also not being fundamentally different from my Copenhagen lifestyle. The canals, the beautiful architecture and the location as a European hotspot inspired my final pick.

On top of that, the chance to take advanced private law courses on UVA was a dream of mine. The many talented lecturers within the Master European Private Law (LLM) programme caught my intention already before choosing UVA, and I was eager to dig into the details of private law within this setting. Having international classmates and learning within a multinational academic community was a fantastic opportunity in my opinion.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
My exchange trip to Amsterdam has been an overwhelmingly positive experience, filled with enriching moments that have left an mark on my personal and academic journey. One of the highlights has undoubtedly been the friendships formed along the way and developing friendships with people from all countries. 

However, the journey has not been without its challenges, particularly on the academic front. UvA's rigorous school curriculum and high expectations definitely tested my abilities and pushed me beyond my comfort zone. It was very challenging having to choose between friendships, experiences among others versus my studies. 

In conclusion, my exchange trip has been an overwhelmingly positive experience, marked by the formation of lasting friendships and a deep immersion into the Dutch culture. The academic challenges, while demanding, also contributed to my personal development.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Finding the obligatory information upon arrival was quite a challenge in itself. I found that there were many different deadlines on different webpages, so you definitely had to be committed. Luckily, I was in a place where I didn't oversee to many deadlines or important means of information, but it was quite a puzzle. For a short recap I had to deliver different informations and documents on UCPH (via both KUnet, MobilityOnline, and via. outlook) and on UvA (via. Outlook, SIS, canvas, etc.)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't really get any assistance. However, I did find that the school were good at informing the students about contact information etc. Also, because we were many exchange students at my chosen destination, it was easy for me to reach out and "use" each other.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy finding housing. Luckily, I got housing through my host institution. However, it was quite far from the university and the city I chose and not great neither.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus is fine, and many exchange students live off campus. However I would recommend future exchange students to look into housing location and other factors. Living in an unpleasant environment definitely affects your overall stay, and I was quite unhappy about my housing situation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was mostly done through my home institution (KU) - hence the process was quite easy. The most challenging aspect was probably delivering documents, certificates etc. before deadlines and keeping track of deadlines. If you're going on a solo exchange trip, I could imagine that you would have to be very structured and committed to your journey.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: KU had an e-mail that you could reach out to, and vice versa at UvA.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was quite succesfull and got about 80% of the courses I initially wanted. However, choosing courses and trying to figure out which courses were actually provided was quite a task and I had to sign up for quite a few and consult with my fellow exchange students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advice you to see the exam form and check the different academic programmes. It was my impression that changing courses were not that hard, so definitely talk to non exchange students for recommendations.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very challenging, and I would advice new exchange students at UvA (especially law students) to ask themselves if they're going to Amsterdam for the academically challenging (and rewarding) programmes or the dutch culture/"wild" exchange student life. It was quite hard to combine the both due to the many school hours.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was very high with way to much literature. One thing is the challenge which lies in studying english law literature. But the literature lists were challenging and long as well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The teaching style at UvA was a bit different than UCPH. One striking difference was UvA's emphasis on attendance and active participation; UvA placed greater expectations on regular attendance and active engagement in class discussions.

This shift requires a recalibration of study habits and participation levels. The heightened expectations compelled me to be more disciplined in attending classes regularly and actively contributing to discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Advanced Private Law
- International Investment Law
- International Trade Law
- Comparative Law
- Consumer rights in a Digital Single Market

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Consumer rights in a Digital Single Market and Advanced Private Law. International Investment Law and International Trade Law were two very challenging courses with quite a work load.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many sport clubs and social + creative activities to join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately, I didn't join any non-academic activities that UvA provided. However, many people were positive about the creative courses at CREA. I did find that the work load at school was very demanding and consequently, I didn't find the time to participate in such activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
To my fellow students, I wholeheartedly recommend Amsterdam as a must-visit destination.

Firstly, I would recommend exploring the city by boat; strolling through neighborhoods like Jordaan, and discovering hidden gems in De Pijp. Secondly, the city is full of historical (and newer) museums. Most notably, the Rijksmuseum and the Anne Frank House, which are almost obligatory to visit.

Overall, Amsterdam has a welcoming and open-minded atmosphere, which is evident when you visit the many cafes and night clubs. Amsterdam has a perfect balance of excitement and relaxation. It's a city that not only broadens your cultural horizons but also houses many night clubs and cool bars, if you're an outgoing and very social person.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Adjusting to the local culture in Amsterdam was hard in the beginning due to the fact that Dutch people tend to keep to themselves. Initially, integration required effort. However, as I actively immersed myself in local activities, eg. joining cycle classes and yoga classes and visited local cafes with a book, the adjustment process became a bit smoother. In the beginning, I also found Amsterdam to be a great city to explore by yourself.

Attending local markets, cultural festivals, and community gatherings with fellow exchange students also provided insight into the local way of life. I quickly established a weekend routine that included these activities, which overall helped me foster a sense of belonging.

My number one tip would be to team up with fellow exchange students!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found the Dutch people's mix of openness (or straightforwardness) and their tendency to keep them to themselves to be particularly challenging. While generally open and approachable, the Dutch also tend to maintain a degree of personal space and reserve, which initially posed a challenge in forming immediate connections with local people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
I most appreciated the unique aspects of Dutch culture and the everyday life. I cherished the local markets, which quickly became a weekend ritual. Overall, Amsterdam has a great ambiance with beautiful canals and historic architecture, which provided some "beauty" to the everyday life.

Moreover, discovering local hotspots, such as hidden cafes and trendy neighborhoods like De Pjip or Oost added excitement to my stay. Clubbing and the social scene in Amsterdam were also highlights of my experience, and I really appreciated trying out the Dutch nightlife with fellow exchange students. The city boasts a diverse and inclusive club culture with a lot of techno scenes and aspiring DJs, which is different from the Copenhagen club culture, where the clubs can be quite similar.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Prepare for Academic Rigor:
Be ready for a higher level of academic intensity. The coursework might demand extensive reading and a deeper engagement with the subject matter. Ensure you're well-organized and manage your time effectively to meet the academic expectations.

2) Engage in Intro Activities:
Attend the introductory activities offered by the host institution. I regret I didn't as this is an excellent way to establish a solid network of acquaintances early on. 

3) Embrace Everyday Life in Amsterdam and UvA's Environment:
Don't just focus on academics; immerse yourself in the vibrant everyday life of Amsterdam. Explore the local markets, cycle along the canals, and savor the unique atmosphere. Additionally, make the most of the environment at UvA; engage in extracurricular activities, join clubs, and participate in events to enrich your overall experience beyond the classroom.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Opt for courses that align with your interests as you'll be dedicating a significant amount of time to studying.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The most rewarding aspect of my exchange experience was probably - although it is a stereotypical answer - my personal growth. Immersing myself in a new culture, navigating different academic approaches, and forming connections with people from all over the world contributed significantly to my personal development. It was very rewarding to learn that you can establish a different life in a new city while meeting a lot of kind people.

Enhancing my English skills was another rewarding aspect. Engaging in academic discussions, social interactions, and day-to-day communication in English not only refined my language proficiency but also boosted my confidence in English.

Lastly, being in Amsterdam itself was a source of continuous reward. Exploring the city; strolling down the canals, biking to school, indulging in local cuisine (especially surinamese cuisine) and reading at cafes by myself, added value to my overall experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The greatest challenge I faced during the exchange was the academic rigor, with courses proving to be more challenging than anticipated. The workload, particularly the extensive reading and demanding assignments in International Investment Law and International Trade Law surpassed my initial expectations. The academic environment at my host institution demanded a higher level of engagement and dedication, requiring me to adapt quickly to the intensity of the coursework. It bears mention that I did choose Master courses only, which probably added to the work load.

Balancing academic commitments with the desire to explore Amsterdam with other exchange students became quite a challenge as it required meticulous time management and prioritization.

Despite the difficulty, overcoming these challenges added a layer of accomplishment to my exchange journey, contributing significantly to my academic development.
